title: Caviar & Crème Fraîche Board
h1: Caviar & Crème Fraîche Board for Two
seo_title: Caviar Board for Two: Blini, Crème Fraîche & What to Buy
description: A caviar board for two: caviar or trout roe on ice, crème fraîche, smoked salmon, mini blini or potato chips, chopped egg, shallot, chives and lemon, with Champagne.
hook: One tin, two spoons, zero regrets: the classic caviar service, scaled down for a night at home.

items.name: Red onion or shallot, finely minced

why: The garnishes on a caviar board are there to stretch one small tin: cool crème fraîche, chopped egg whites and yolks, minced shallot and chives. Each one changes the bite a little, and none of them hide the roe.
Mini blini are traditional, but thin, plain potato chips are a favorite modern swap. Smoked salmon makes it filling, and brut Champagne or ice-cold vodka is the classic pour.

timeline.what: Hard-boil and chill the eggs; chill the Champagne or vodka.
Chop the egg, onion and chives into separate small bowls.
Warm the blini at 350°F for 3–4 minutes.
Set the caviar tin on ice; build the board.
Open the tin at the table.

faq.q: How much caviar do you need for two?
faq.a: About 30 g (1 oz) is a generous tasting for two. Trout or salmon roe lets you serve more for less.

faq.q: What do you serve with caviar?
faq.a: Blini or plain potato chips, crème fraîche, chopped hard-boiled egg, minced shallot or red onion, chives and lemon, with Champagne or vodka.

faq.q: How do you keep caviar cold?
faq.a: Set the tin on crushed ice and open it right before serving. Use a bone, mother-of-pearl or plastic spoon; metal can give it a slight off taste.
